gel-comb.context: A flat bar with three teeth hanging down, the tool pressed into liquid gel to leave sample wells. Used for electrophoresis, DNA analysis and molecular biology lab content.

uv-transilluminator.context: A low light box with a gel slab on top and short rays shining above it. Used for viewing DNA bands in stained gels in molecular biology and imaging content.

centrifuge-pellet.context: A conical tube with a dark pellet at its tip and a curved arrow beside it. Used for centrifugation, sample separation and spin-down steps in lab protocols.

electroporation.context: A round cell with gaps in its membrane and a dot inside, next to a lightning bolt. Used for electrical gene delivery, transfection and cell engineering topics.

microfluidic-chip.context: A small rounded chip with a winding channel running between two round ports. Used for lab-on-a-chip devices, microfluidics and diagnostics content.

bioprinter.context: A printer nozzle above a row of small dots and a flat plate. Used for 3D bioprinting, tissue engineering and regenerative medicine content.

microscope-objective.context: A stepped lens barrel narrowing to a tip with a single drop below it. Used for microscopy optics, oil immersion and magnification topics.

tissue-cassette.context: A flat box with a slanted front edge and three slots in its lid. Used for histology, pathology and biopsy tissue processing content.

durham-tube.context: A test tube with a small upside-down tube inside it, the sign of trapped gas. Used for bacterial fermentation tests and microbiology lab teaching.

loop-sterilizer.context: A short heater box with an inoculation loop wire held above its opening. Used for sterilizing loops in microbiology and aseptic technique content.

lab-mouse-cage.context: A box cage with a wire lid and a small mouse inside. Used for animal research facilities, rodent studies and vivarium content.

fly-vial.context: A narrow vial with a foam plug on top, a food layer at the bottom and two flies inside. Used for fruit fly genetics and Drosophila research content.

cryo-electron-grid.context: A small round disc crossed by a fine square mesh. Used for cryo-EM sample preparation and electron microscopy topics.

pycnometer.context: A round-bottomed bottle with a thin neck and a stopper that has a hole through it. Used for measuring density and specific gravity in chemistry and materials labs.

thiele-tube.context: A rectangular glass loop with a short chimney on top, a thermometer standing in it. Used for melting point tests and oil bath heating in chemistry teaching.

melting-point-apparatus.context: A compact box with a round viewing lens and three tubes standing in its top. Used for melting point measurement and sample purity checks in chemistry labs.

microbial-air-sampler.context: A round perforated sampler head above a stem and an open agar dish. Used for air quality testing, cleanroom monitoring and contamination control.

water-sample-bottle.context: A wide bottle with a cap and a label band, under a tap with one drop falling. Used for water testing, environmental sampling and public health content.

roller-bottle.context: A long cylindrical bottle lying on its side with a short neck, resting on two small rollers. Used for large-scale cell culture and bioprocessing content.

square-archaeon.context: A flat square cell with thin walls and three small oval gas vesicles inside. Used for archaea, extremophiles and unusual microbe content.

myxobacteria-fruiting-body.context: A short stalk that branches into three, each branch topped by a round spore ball. Used for myxobacteria, bacterial development and microbial cooperation topics.

phage-plaque-assay.context: A round dish seen from above with a dotted lawn and a few clear circles where viruses killed bacteria. Used for bacteriophage counting and virology teaching.

bacterial-transformation.context: A rod-shaped bacterium with a small ring outside and a curved arrow pointing into the cell. Used for plasmid uptake, cloning and genetic engineering topics.

spore-germination.context: An open oval spore with a thin branching thread growing out of the split end. Used for fungal spores, mould growth and microbial life cycle content.

nuclear-pore.context: A round ring with a central hole and eight spokes between the hole and the outer edge. Used for the nuclear envelope, molecular transport and cell biology teaching.

proteasome.context: An upright barrel made of stacked rings with a bar at each end and a thin wavy chain entering the top. Used for protein degradation, ubiquitin and cell recycling topics.

atp-synthase.context: A lobed knob head on a short stalk above a wide rotor block, with a curved arrow around it. Used for ATP production, mitochondria and bioenergetics teaching.

krebs-cycle.context: A ring of curved arrows with a dot at each of four steps and a short arrow entering at the top. Used for the citric acid cycle and metabolism teaching.

cellular-respiration.context: A bean-shaped mitochondrion with a zigzag inner membrane, under a hexagon sugar ring and a lightning bolt. Used for glucose to energy conversion and biology teaching.

oxytocin-molecule.context: A six-sided ring of beads with a bridge across one corner and a short tail of beads. Used for the bonding hormone, neuropeptides and biochemistry content.

reagent-reservoir.context: A shallow open trough with one sloped end and a wavy liquid line inside. Used for multichannel pipetting, liquid handling and assay prep.

microplate-reader.context: A boxy instrument with a small display and indicator dots above an open drawer holding a well plate. Used for ELISA, absorbance assays and lab automation.

amplification-curve.context: A graph with two S-shaped curves climbing from the baseline past a dashed threshold line. Used for real-time PCR results and DNA quantification topics.

aseptic-technique.context: A tilted open tube with its mouth over a small flame, and a small cap held to one side. Used for sterile transfer methods in microbiology teaching.

dialysis-tubing.context: A clipped bag hanging on a string in a beaker, with small dots drifting out through its wall. Used for diffusion, osmosis and semipermeable membrane teaching.
